title: O God! to Thee Our Hearts Would Pay
description: O God! to Thee Our Hearts Would Pay in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 401, “Close of the Year”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God! to Thee our hearts would pay Their grat-i-tude sin-cere, Whose love hath kept us, night and day, Through-out an-oth-er year.

lines: O God! to Thee our hearts would pay
Whose love hath kept us, night and day,
Of every breath, and every power,
From Thee came every happy hour
And if sometimes across our path
Thou didst not waft it there in wrath,
For joy and grief alike we pay
And only pray to grow each day

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
